paragraphs: Ryerson Holding Corporation ("Ryerson Holding"), a Delaware corporation, is the parent company of Joseph T. Ryerson & Son, Inc. ("JT Ryerson"), a Delaware corporation. As of December 31, 2025, affiliates of Platinum Equity, LLC ("Platinum") own approximately 3,924,478 shares of our common stock, which is approximately 12.2% of our issued and outstanding common stock.

We are a leading value-added processor and distributor of industrial metals with operations in the United States ("U.S.") through JT Ryerson and other U.S. subsidiaries, in Canada through our indirect wholly-owned subsidiary Ryerson Canada, Inc., a Canadian corporation ("Ryerson Canada"), and in Mexico through our indirect wholly-owned subsidiary Ryerson Metals de Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V., a Mexican corporation ("Ryerson Mexico"). In addition to our North American operations, we conduct metal processing and distribution operations in China through an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary, Ryerson China Limited, a Chinese limited liability company ("Ryerson China"). Unless the context indicates otherwise, Ryerson Holding, JT Ryerson, Ryerson Canada, Ryerson Mexico, and Ryerson China together with their subsidiaries, are collectively referred to herein as "Ryerson," "we," "us," "our," or the "Company."

We are one of the largest value-add processors and distributors of industrial metals in North America measured in terms of sales. As of December 31, 2025, we have approximately 4,300 employees across 103 facilities in North America and three facilities in China. Through this network we serve approximately 40,000 customers across a wide range of manufacturing end-markets. Our customers range from local, independently owned fabricators and machine shops to large, international original equipment manufacturers. We carry a full line of approximately 75,000 products in stainless steel, aluminum, carbon steel, and alloy steels and a limited line of nickel and red metals in various shapes and forms. In addition to our metals products, we offer numerous value-added processing and fabrication services, and nearly 80% of the products we sell are processed to meet customer requirements.

Our business strategy includes providing a superior level of customer service and responsiveness, technical services, and inventory management solutions while maintaining low operating costs in order to maximize financial results. Our growth strategy is based on increasing our operating results through organic growth activities and strategic acquisitions.

To that end, we continue to focus on our interconnected network, systems, and enhancing our value-added services and online presence to provide increased access, functionality, and flexibility to our customers. We are using advanced analytics to improve pricing and inventory utilization. Our service centers are strategically located near our customers, which permits us to quickly process and deliver our products and services, often the day after receiving an order. We own, lease, or contract a fleet of tractors and trailers, allowing us to efficiently meet our customers' delivery demands. Our range of products together with our breadth of services allows us to service a diverse customer base and to create long-term partnerships with our customers and enhances our profitability.

We focus on strategic acquisitions that complement and enhance our product, customer, and geographic diversification. Ryerson's M&A strategy includes both transformative turnaround acquisitions and value-add, bolt-on acquisitions. On October 28, 2025, Ryerson and Olympic Steel, Inc. ("Olympic Steel") jointly announced their definitive agreement to merge and on February 13, 2026, they announced the successful completion of the merger (the "Olympic Steel Merger"). Olympic Steel is a metals service center focused on the direct sale and value-added processing of carbon and coated sheet, plate, and coil products; stainless steel sheet, plate, bar, and coil; aluminum sheet, plate, and coil; pipe, tube, bar, valves and fittings, tin plate and metal-intensive end-use products. Olympic Steel provides metals processing and distribution services for a wide range of customers. The combination of the two companies enhances Ryerson's presence as North America's second largest metals service center, bringing Olympic Steel's complementary footprint, capabilities, and product offering into Ryerson's intelligently interconnected network of value-added service centers. Please refer to the Section titled "Olympic Steel Acquisition" of Item 7, Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Conditions and Results of Operations," and Note 19 — "Subsequent Events" of Part II, Item 8 "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" for further information on the Olympic Steel Merger. In 2024 and 2023, Ryerson focused on bolt-on acquisitions. In 2024, we acquired Production Metals, LLC while in 2023, Ryerson's acquisitions included BLP Holdings, LLC, Norlen Incorporated, TSA Processing, and Hudson Tool Steel Corporation.

Metals service centers serve as key intermediaries between metal producers and end users of metal products. They purchase in scale and sell in smaller quantities. End-users often look for "one-stop" suppliers that offer lower order volumes, shorter lead times, more reliable delivery, and processing services. Metal producers mainly sell metals in the form of standard-sized coils, sheets, plates,

structurals, bars, and tubes in large quantities, with longer lead times and limited inventory. Metal service centers serve as key intermediaries closing the gap between metal producers' supply and end-users' demand.

By aggregating end-users' demand and purchasing metal in bulk to take advantage of economies of scale, metals service centers may purchase, process, and deliver metal to end‑users in a more efficient and cost‑effective manner than the end‑user may achieve by dealing directly with the primary producer. Further, specialized metals processing equipment is costly and requires high‑volume production to be cost effective, and many customers are not able or willing to invest in the necessary technology, equipment, and warehousing of inventory to efficiently and effectively perform metal processing for their own operations. Due to this, many customers have reduced their in-house processing capabilities, opting to source processed metal from service centers like us. This saves our customers time, labor, and expense, reducing their overall manufacturing costs. It also permits us to increasingly focus on value-added services and expansion of our mix of fabricated products, which typically sell at higher margins. We therefore invest in our processing equipment to grow this mix and our gross profit margin.

Our industry is highly fragmented with the largest companies accounting for only a small percentage of total market share. The majority of metals services companies have limited product lines and inventories and their customers are usually located within their local geographic area. In general, competition is based on quality, service, price, and geographic proximity. We primarily compete with other metals service centers and to a lesser extent with metal producers.

The metals service center industry typically experiences cash flow trends that are counter-cyclical to the revenue and volume growth of the industry. During an industry downturn, companies generally reduce working capital assets and generate cash as inventory and accounts receivable balances decline, and as a result, operating cash flow and liquidity tend to increase during a downturn.

Based on sales, we are one of the largest service center companies for carbon, stainless steel, and aluminum in the North American market where we have a broad geographic presence with 103 facilities, as of December 31, 2025.

Our service centers are located near our customer locations, enabling us to timely deliver to customers across numerous geographic markets. Additionally, our widespread network of locations in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico helps us to utilize our expertise to efficiently serve customers with complex supply chain requirements across multiple manufacturing locations. We believe this is a key differentiator for customers who need a supplier that can reliably and consistently support them. Our ability to transfer inventory among our facilities better enables us to timely and profitably source and process specialized items at regional locations throughout our network than if we were required to maintain inventory of all products and specialized equipment at each location.

Our operations serve a diverse range of industries including commercial transportation, fabrication and welding, machinery and equipment, consumer products, heavy equipment, climate, power, and machine shop sectors. We believe this broad range of industries in which we sell our products and services reduces our risk related to a downturn in a specific industry. We believe that our ability to quickly adjust our offerings based on regional and industry specific trends creates stability while also providing the opportunity to access specific growth markets. We are focused on expanding our presence within growing, secular markets, including electric vehicles and renewable energy.

headings: Weakness in the economy, market trends, and other conditions affecting the profitability and financial stability of our customers has and could continue to negatively impact our sales growth and results of operations.
The metals services business is very competitive and increased competition has and could reduce our revenues and gross margins.
Changing metals prices have a significant impact on our liquidity, net sales, gross margins, operating income, and net income.
Unexpected product shortages could negatively impact customer relationships, resulting in an adverse impact on results of operations.
Changes in customer or product mix could cause our gross margin percentage to decline.
We may not be able to retain or expand our customer base if the North American manufacturing industry erodes through acquisition and merger or consolidation activity in our customers' industries.

Global metal overcapacity and imports of metal products into the United States have adversely affected, and may again adversely affect, United States metal prices, which could impact our sales and results of operations.
Lead time and the cost of our products could increase if we were to lose one of our primary suppliers.
The volatility of the market could result in a material impairment of goodwill.
Changes in inflation have and may continue to adversely affect financial performance.
We may be unable to successfully integrate our and Olympic Steel's businesses in order to realize the anticipated benefits of the Olympic Steel Merger or do so within the intended timeframe.
Certain of our operations are located outside of the United States, which subjects us to risks associated with international activities.
We may be adversely affected by currency fluctuations in the U.S. dollar versus the Canadian dollar, the Chinese renminbi, the Hong Kong dollar, and the Mexican peso.
The Chinese government exerts substantial influence over the manner in which we must conduct our business activities, particularly with regards to the land our facilities are located on.
Damage to our information technology infrastructure could harm our business.

We are subject to cybersecurity risks and other vulnerabilities that could arise with the sophistication and heightened use of artificial intelligence and may incur increasing costs in an effort to minimize those risks.
The use or anticipated use of artificial intelligence technologies by us or third parties may increase operational risks or create new or unanticipated operational risks.
Any significant work stoppages can harm our business.
Certain employee retirement benefit plans are underfunded and the actual cost of those benefits could exceed current estimates, which would require us to fund the shortfall.
Any prolonged disruption of our processing centers could harm our business.
If we are unable to retain, attract, and motivate management and key personnel, it may adversely affect our business.
Our risk management strategies may result in losses.
We could incur substantial costs related to environmental, health, and safety laws.
Environmental, social, and governance matters, and any related reporting obligation may impact our business.
Tax changes could affect our effective tax rate, the value of our deferred tax assets, and future profitability.
We are subject to litigation that could strain our resources and distract management.
We may face product liability claims that are costly and create adverse publicity.
Our stock price has fluctuated in the past, has recently been volatile, and may be volatile in the future, and as a result, investors in our common stock could incur substantial losses.
We paid cash dividends on our common stock in each quarter of 2025, but any future dividend payments are at the discretion of our Board of Directors.
Our corporate documents and Delaware law contain provisions that could discourage, delay, or prevent a change in control of the Company.

Any issuance of preferred stock could make it difficult for another company to acquire us or could otherwise adversely affect holders of our common stock, which could depress the price of our common stock.
We have indebtedness under our Ryerson Credit Facility, which could adversely affect our financial position and prevent us from fulfilling our financial obligations.

The covenants in the Ryerson Credit Facility and covenants contained in agreements governing indebtedness that we incur in the future may impose restrictions that may limit our operating and financial flexibility.
We may not be able to generate sufficient cash to service all of our indebtedness.
Because all of our indebtedness bears interest at rates that fluctuate with changes in certain prevailing short-term interest rates, we are vulnerable to interest rate increases.
Changes in our credit ratings and outlook may reduce access to capital and increase borrowing costs.
paragraphs: Our business faces many risks. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, together with the other information in this report, including the consolidated financial statements and notes to the consolidated financial statements. We cannot assure you that any of the events discussed in the risk factors below will not occur. These risks could have a material and adverse impact on our business, results of operations, financial condition, and cash flows.

Economic and industry trends affect our business environments. We serve several metals-consuming industries in which the demand for our products and services is sensitive to the production activity, capital spending, and demand for products and services of our customers. Many of these customers operate in markets that are subject to highly cyclical fluctuations resulting from seasonality, market uncertainty, costs of goods sold, currency exchange rates, foreign competition, offshoring of production, oil and natural gas prices, geopolitical developments, and a variety of other factors beyond our control. Any of these factors have and could cause customers to idle or close facilities, delay purchases, reduce production levels, or experience reductions in the demand for their own products or services.

Any of these events could impair the ability of our customers to make full and timely payments or reduce the volume of products and services these customers purchase from us and could cause increased pressure on our selling prices and terms of sale. We do not expect the cyclical nature of our customer base to change and any downturn in our customers' industries could reduce our revenues and profitability or a significant or prolonged slowdown in activity in the U.S., Canada, or any other major world economy, or a segment of any such economy, could negatively impact our sales growth and results of operations.

We face competition in all markets we serve, from metals producers that sell directly to certain customers or segments of the market, to other metal services companies. The metals services industry itself is highly fragmented and competitive. There are a few

large competitors, but most of the market is served by small local and regional competitors. Competition is based principally on price, service, quality, production capabilities, inventory availability, and timely delivery.

We are experiencing increased pressure from online businesses that compete with price transparency. We expect technological advancements and the increased use of e-commerce solutions within the industry to continue to evolve at a rapid pace. As a result, our ability to effectively compete requires us to respond and adapt to new industry trends and developments, and implement new technology and innovations that may result in unexpected costs or may take longer than expected.

This section of this Form 10-K generally discusses 2025 and 2024 items and year-over-year comparisons between 2025 and 2024. Discussions of 2023 items and year-over-year comparisons between 2024 and 2023 that are not included in this Form 10-K can be found in "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7 of the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024.

Ryerson Holding Corporation ("Ryerson Holding"), a Delaware corporation, is the parent company of Joseph T. Ryerson & Son, Inc. ("JT Ryerson"), a Delaware corporation. As of December 31, 2025 affiliates of Platinum Equity, LLC ("Platinum") own approximately 3,924,478 shares of our common stock, which is approximately 12.2% of our issued and outstanding common stock.

We are a leading value-added processor and distributor of industrial metals with operations in the United States ("U.S.") through JT Ryerson and other U.S. subsidiaries, in Canada through our indirect wholly-owned subsidiary Ryerson Canada, Inc., a Canadian corporation ("Ryerson Canada"), and in Mexico through our indirect wholly-owned subsidiary Ryerson Metals de Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V., a Mexican corporation ("Ryerson Mexico"). In addition to our North American operations, we conduct metal processing and distribution operations in China through an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary, Ryerson China Limited, a Chinese limited liability company ("Ryerson China"). Unless the context indicates otherwise, Ryerson Holding, JT Ryerson, Ryerson Canada, Ryerson Mexico, and Ryerson China together with their subsidiaries, are collectively referred to herein as "Ryerson," "we," "us," "our," or the "Company."

We are a metals service center providing value-added processing and distribution of industrial metals with operations in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, and China. We purchase large quantities of metal products from primary producers and sell these materials in smaller quantities to a wide variety of metals-consuming industries. We carry a full line of approximately 75,000 products in stainless steel, aluminum, carbon steel, and alloy steels and a limited line of nickel and red metals in various shapes and forms. In addition to our metals products, we offer numerous value-added processing and fabrication services, and nearly 80% of the metals products we sell are processed by us by bending, beveling, blanking, blasting, burning, cutting-to-length, drilling, flattening, forming, grinding, laser cutting, machining, notching, painting, polishing, punching, rolling, sawing, shearing, slitting, stamping, tapping, threading, welding, or other techniques to process materials to a specified thickness, length, width, shape, and surface quality pursuant to specific customer orders.

Similar to other metals service centers, we maintain substantial inventories of metals to accommodate the short lead times and just-in-time delivery requirements of our customers. Accordingly, we purchase metals to maintain our inventory at levels that we believe to be appropriate to satisfy the anticipated needs of our customers based upon customer forecasts, historic buying practices, supply agreements with customers, mill lead times, and market conditions. Our commitments to purchase metals are generally at prevailing market prices in effect at the time we place our orders. At the request of our customers, we have some fixed price sales contracts. We have entered into swaps in order to mitigate our risk of volatility in the price of metals related to these contracts and we have entered into metals hedges to mitigate our own risk of volatility in the price of metals. We have no long-term, fixed-price metals purchase contracts. When metals prices decline, customer demands for lower prices and our competitors' responses to those demands could result in lower sale prices and, consequently, lower gross profits and earnings as we sell existing metals inventory. When metals prices increase, competitive conditions will influence how much of the price increase we may pass on to our customers.

The metals service center industry is cyclical and volatile in both demand and pricing, and difficult to predict. In 2025, Ryerson experienced marginal volume growth of 0.5% and an average selling price decrease of 1.1% compared to 2024 as the period was characterized by subdued downstream demand and volatile pricing, impacted by tariff trade policy. Changes in average selling prices are primarily driven by commodity metals prices, which impact Ryerson's selling prices over the subsequent three to six-month period.

In 2025, indicators for key steel industry end markets reported contraction in industrial activity momentum but output improvement relative to the previous year. This is evidenced by the Institute for Supply Management's Purchasing Managers' Index ("PMI"), which indicated that the majority of surveyed purchasing managers reported a decline in activity in nearly every month of 2025 with the exception of January and February, as marked by readings below the growth threshold of 50. January 2026 reversed the trend with a reading above the growth threshold of 52.6. On the other hand, U.S. Industrial Production, which reports year-over-year industrial sector business output, reported growth for each month of 2025, indicating that while PMI would suggest that 2025 was a year of widespread contractionary momentum, there was resiliency in the overall output relative to the previous year.

According to the Metal Service Center Institute, North American service center volumes decreased by 1.5% in 2025 compared to 2024. Also on a North American basis, Ryerson's volumes declined by 0.4% over the same period, implying that the Company gained market share during the year. Reflecting on volume performance by end-market, Ryerson experienced year-over-year declines in Commercial Transportation, Climate, Heavy Equipment, and Power sectors. These declines were partially offset by demand growth in Fabrication & Welding, Machine Shop, and Machinery & Equipment sectors.

On February 13, 2026 (the "Closing Date"), the Company completed the transactions contemplated by the Agreement and Plan of Merger, (the "Merger Agreement"), dated as of October 28, 2025, by and among Ryerson Holding, Crimson MS Corp., an Ohio corporation and a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Ryerson Holding ("Merger Sub"), and Olympic Steel, Inc. ("Olympic Steel"). On the Closing Date, pursuant to the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub merged with and into Olympic Steel in accordance with Ohio law. At the effective time of the Olympic Steel Merger, each issued and outstanding share of common stock of Olympic Steel, without par per share (the "Olympic Common Stock") (other than certain excluded shares), was converted into the right to receive 1.7105 shares the Ryerson Holding's common stock, rounded down to the nearest whole share, and cash in lieu of fractional shares. Upon the completion of the Olympic Steel Merger, Olympic Steel, as the surviving corporation, became a wholly owned subsidiary of Ryerson Holding. As a result of the Olympic Steel Merger, Ryerson Holding issued approximately 19.5 million shares of its common stock to former holders of Olympic Common Stock

Olympic Steel is a metals service center focused on the direct sale and value-added processing of carbon and coated sheet, plate, and coil products; stainless steel sheet, plate, bar, and coil; aluminum sheet, plate, and coil; pipe, tube, bar, valves and fittings, tin plate, and metal-intensive end-use products. The combination of the two companies enhances Ryerson's presence as North America's second largest metals service center, bringing Olympic Steel's complementary footprint, capabilities, and product offering into Ryerson's intelligently interconnected network of value-added service centers. Together, functioning as Ryerson Holding Corporation, the combined entity is expected to generate approximately $120 million in annual synergies by the beginning of 2028 through procurement scale, efficiency gains, commercial enhancement, and network optimization. Please refer to Note 19 — "Subsequent Events" of Part II, Item 8 "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" for further information on the Olympic Steel merger.

Ryerson's market strategy focuses on providing excellent customer experiences consistently with speed at scale. Our culture is based on our trademarked "say yes, figure it out" mantra. We strive to grow our volume and sustainably expand margins by increasing our fabrication business, transactional sales, and improving our speed through tools and analytics. Ryerson's financial strategy includes a focus on generating cash from operating activities and continuously improving a "through the cycle" operating model to maintain a strong balance sheet, re-invest in the growth of the business, and generate returns to stockholders.

In 2025, coming off of a historically high three-year investment cycle, the Company focused on operationalizing and optimizing major capital investment projects at its service centers in Shelbyville, KY, Norcross, GA, Dallas, TX, and Los Angeles, CA. The primary objective of these investments was to improve Ryerson's operating model and the customer experience. The expansion of our Shelbyville service center, for example, was an investment in our bright metals flat roll processing capabilities to support transactional market share growth at a lower cost to service with improved service levels. Likewise, the investments made in Norcross, Dallas, and Los Angeles included processing equipment, which we expect will improve our ability to provide our customers with higher value-added products and thereby improve our gross margins.

Demand conditions in 2025 continued to be subdued while pricing was volatile, impacted by tariff trade policy. Nonetheless, we believe that the investments that we have made in our service capabilities and operating model will enable us to provide better experiences for our customers and, in turn, enable greater value generation for our stockholders.

paragraphs: Ryerson Holding Corporation ("Ryerson Holding"), 一間 Delaware 公司，為 Joseph T. Ryerson & Son, Inc. ("JT Ryerson"), 一間 Delaware 公司之母公司。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，Platinum Equity, LLC ("Platinum") 之關係企業持有我們約 3,924,478  shares 之普通股，約佔我們已發行及流通普通股之 12.2%。

我們為美國 ("U.S.") 透過 JT Ryerson 及其他美國子公司、加拿大透過我們間接全資擁有之子公司 Ryerson Canada, Inc., 一間加拿大公司 ("Ryerson Canada"), 以及墨西哥透過我們間接全資擁有之子公司 Ryerson Metals de Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V., 一間墨西哥公司 ("Ryerson Mexico") 進行工業金屬之價值增加加工與分銷業務。除了北美業務外，我們亦透過間接全資擁有之子公司 Ryerson China Limited, 一間中國有限責任公司 ("Ryerson China") 在中國進行金屬加工與分銷業務。除非文意另有明示，Ryerson Holding、JT Ryerson、Ryerson Canada、Ryerson Mexico、Ryerson China 以及其子公司，於本文中 collectively 稱為 "Ryerson"、"we"、"us"、"our" 或 "the Company."

我們為北美地區工業金屬價值增加加工與分銷業務之最大業者，以銷售額為衡量標準。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在北美地區與中國共有約 4,300 名員工，分佈於 103 個設施與三個設施。透過此網路，我們服務約 40,000 個客戶，涵蓋廣泛之製造終端市場。我們之客戶從當地獨立擁有之製造商與機械工廠，到大型國際原廠設備製造商皆有。我們擁有約 75,000 種產品之完整線路，包括不銹鋼、鋁、碳鋼與合金鋼，以及有限種鎳與紅金屬，以各種形狀與形式呈現。除了金屬產品外，我們亦提供多種價值增加之加工與製造服務，約有近 80% 之產品為符合客戶需求而進行加工。
我們之業務策略包括提供優越之客戶服務與反應速度、技術服務與存貨管理解決方案，同時維持低營運成本，以最大化財務成果。我們之成長策略係基於透過內生成長活動與戰略收購來提升營運成果。

為此，我們持續著重於我們的 interconnected network、systems，以及提升價值-added services 與 online presence，以提供客戶更高的存取性、功能與靈活性。我們運用 advanced analytics 來改善 pricing 與 inventory utilization。我們的 service centers 設立在靠近客戶的戰略位置，使我們能迅速處理並交付產品與服務，常見的是在收到訂單隔天即可處理與交付。我們擁有、租賃或透過合約取得一隊 tractors 與 trailers，使我們能有效應對客戶的配送需求。我們的產品範圍與服務廣度使我們能服務多樣化的客戶羣體，並與客戶建立長期合作關係，進而提升我們的 profitability。

我們著重於戰略性收購，以補強並提升我們的產品、客戶與地理多元化。Ryerson 的 M&A 策略包括 transformative turnaround 收購與 value-add、bolt-on 收購。2025 年 10 月 28 日，Ryerson 與 Olympic Steel, Inc.（"Olympic Steel"）共同宣佈達成 merger 的最終協議，並於 2026 年 2 月 13 日宣佈 merger 已成功完成（"Olympic Steel Merger"）。Olympic Steel 是一家專注於碳與塗層鋼板、平板、卷材產品；不銹鋼板、平板、棒材與卷材；鋁板、平板與卷材；管、管、棒、閥門與配件、錫板與金屬密集終端用途產品的金屬服務中心，提供金屬加工與配送服務給廣泛的客戶羣。兩家公司結合後，強化了 Ryerson 在北美第二大金屬服務中心的聲勢，將 Olympic Steel 的補充性據點、能力與產品線納入 Ryerson 智能連接的價值-added 服務中心網路。請參閱第 7 節標題為 "Olympic Steel Acquisition" 的 "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Conditions and Results of Operations"，以及第 II 部分第 8 節 "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" 中的 Note 19 — "Subsequent Events"，以取得更多關於 Olympic Steel Merger 的資訊。2024 年與 2023 年，Ryerson 聚焦於 bolt-on 收購。2024 年，我們收購了 Production Metals, LLC，而在 2023 年，Ryerson 的收購包括 BLP Holdings, LLC、Norlen Incorporated、TSA Processing 與 Hudson Tool Steel Corporation。
金屬服務中心是金屬製造商與金屬產品終端用戶之間的關鍵中介。他們以規模購入，並以較小數量銷售。終端用戶常尋求 "one-stop" 供應商，提供較低的訂單數量、較短的交貨時間、更可靠的交貨與加工服務。金屬製造商主要以標準尺寸的卷材、板、平板、結構件、棒與管等大量銷售，交貨時間較長，庫存有限。
金屬服務中心是金屬製造商與終端用戶之間的關鍵中介，彌補金屬製造商供應與終端用戶需求之間的差距。

透過彙整終端用戶的採購需求並以大量採購金屬，金屬服務中心可能以更具效率且成本效益的方式，購買、加工並交付金屬至終端用戶，而終端用戶若直接與主要生產商交易，可能無法達到此效果。此外，專門的金屬加工設備成本高昂，且需高產量才能達到成本效益，許多客戶並無法或不願投資必要的技術、設備與存貨儲存，以有效執行自身的金屬加工作業。因此，許多客戶已減少其內部加工能力，選擇從如我們這類的服務中心取得加工過的金屬。這可為客戶節省時間、人力與費用，降低其整體製造成本。同時也使我們能更專注於附加價值服務與擴大我們的加工產品組合，這些產品通常具有較高的毛利率。我們因此投資於加工設備，以擴大此組合與我們的毛利率。
我們的產業高度分散，最大的公司僅佔總市場份額的一小部分。大多數的金屬服務公司產品線與存貨有限，其客戶通常位於其當地地理區域內。總體而言，競爭主要基於品質、服務、價格與地理距離。我們主要與其他金屬服務中心競爭，次要則與金屬生產商競爭。
金屬服務中心產業通常會經歷與產業營收與產量成長反向的現金流趨勢。在產業低迷時期，公司通常會減少營運資金資產，並因存貨與應收帳款餘額下降而產生現金，因此，營運現金流與流動性通常會在低迷時期增加。
根據銷售額，我們是北美市場中碳鋼、不鏽鋼與鋁合金服務中心中規模最大的公司之一，我們在該地區擁有廣泛的地理分佈，截至2025年12月31日，共有103個據點。

我們的服務中心位於客戶所在地附近，使我們能及時交付至多個地理區域的客戶。此外，我們在美國、加拿大與墨西哥的廣泛據點網路，使我們能運用專業知識，有效服務具有複雜供應鏈需求的客戶，並覆蓋多個製造據點。我們認為這對需要可靠且穩定供應商的客戶而言，是一項關鍵優勢。我們能於各據點間轉移存貨的能力，使我們能更有效地於整個網路的區域據點進行專門品項的採購與加工，這比我們必須在每個據點維持所有產品與專門設備的存貨更具效益。
我們的業務服務多樣化的產業，包括商業運輸、製造與焊接、機械與設備、消費性產品、重型設備、氣候、能源與機械工廠等產業。我們認為我們銷售產品與服務的廣泛產業範疇，可降低特定產業低迷所帶來的風險。我們認為我們能根據區域與產業特定趨勢快速調整服務內容，這不僅能創造穩定性，同時也提供我們進入特定成長市場的機會。我們專注於擴大在成長性、長遠市場的佈局，包括電動車與再生能源。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析應與瑞森控股公司及其子公司經審計之合併財務報表及附註（第 8 項「財務報表與補充資料」）一併閱讀。此討論包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性。請參閱「關於前瞻性陳述之特別說明」一節。我們實際結果與特定事件的時間點可能與這些前瞻性陳述中所討論者有重大差異，原因包括某些因素，包括在第 1A 項「風險因素」及其他此 Form 10-K 中所討論者。
此 Form 10-K 本節一般討論 2025 年與 2024 年項目及 2025 年與 2024 年之年對年比較。未包含於此 Form 10-K 中之 2023 年項目及 2024 年與 2023 年之年對年比較，可於本公司於 2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度之年度報告 Form 10-K 中第 II 項第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」中找到。
瑞森控股公司（「瑞森控股」），為德拉瓦州公司，為約瑟夫·T·瑞森與子有限公司（「JT 瑞森」），為德拉瓦州公司之母公司。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，Platinum Equity, LLC（「Platinum」）之關係企業持有我們約 3,924,478 股普通股，約為我們發行與流通普通股之 12.2%。

我們為一家領先的增值加工與分銷工業金屬之公司，於美國（「美國」）透過 JT 瑞森及其他美國子公司運作，在加拿大透過我們間接全資擁有之子公司瑞森加拿大有限公司（「瑞森加拿大」），為加拿大公司，在墨西哥透過我們間接全資擁有之子公司瑞森金屬墨西哥股份有限公司（「瑞森墨西哥」），為墨西哥公司。除了我們在北美之運作，我們亦在中國透過間接全資擁有之子公司瑞森中國有限公司，為中國有限責任公司（「瑞森中國」）進行金屬加工與分銷運作。除非上下文另有說明，瑞森控股、JT 瑞森、瑞森加拿大、瑞森墨西哥與瑞森中國及其子公司，於此文中 collectively 稱為「瑞森」、「我們」、「我們」、「我們」或「本公司」。

我們為一家金屬服務中心，提供工業金屬之增值加工與分銷運作，於美國、加拿大、墨西哥與中國運作。我們從主要生產商購入大量金屬產品，並以較小數量銷售給多種金屬消費產業。我們持有約 75,000 種產品之完整線路，包括不銹鋼、鋁、碳鋼與合金鋼，以及有限種鎳與紅金屬，以各種形狀與形式呈現。除了我們之金屬產品，我們亦提供眾多增值加工與製造服務，且我們約 80% 之金屬產品銷售為我們加工，透過彎曲、斜邊、衝壓、噴砂、切割、鑽孔、壓平、成型、磨削、雷射切割、機械加工、切口、噴漆、拋光、衝壓、滾壓、切割、剪切、分條、衝壓、攻牙、螺紋、焊接或其他技術，根據特定客戶訂單將材料加工至指定厚度、長度、寬度、形狀與表面品質。

與其他金屬服務中心相似，我們維持大量金屬庫存，以符合客戶短交期與即時配送之需求。因此，我們購入金屬以維持庫存量於我們認為適當之水準，以滿足客戶預期需求，基於客戶預測、歷史採購模式、與客戶之供應協議、廠家交貨時間與市場條件。我們對購入金屬之承諾通常為當時市場價格。應客戶要求，我們有部分固定價格銷售契約。我們已簽訂期貨合約以降低與這些契約相關之金屬價格波動風險，並已簽訂金屬避險以降低我們自身之金屬價格波動風險。我們沒有長期固定價格之金屬採購契約。當金屬價格下跌時，客戶對較低價格之需求與我們競爭對手對此需求之回應，可能導致銷售價格降低，進而導致毛利率與獲利降低，因我們銷售現有金屬庫存。當金屬價格上漲時，競爭條件將影響我們能將多少價格上漲轉嫁給客戶。
金屬服務中心產業為週期性且價格波動性大，且難以預測。2025 年，瑞森經歷 0.5% 之小幅營業額成長與 1.1% 之平均銷售價格下降，與 2024 年相比，因該期間特徵為下游需求低迷與價格波動，受關稅貿易政策影響。平均銷售價格之變動主要由原物料金屬價格驅動，此影響瑞森之銷售價格於隨後三個至六個月期間。

2025 年，關鍵鋼鐵產業終端市場指標顯示工業活動動能收縮，但相較於前一年之產出改善。此由供應管理協會（Institute for Supply Management）之採購經理指數（「PMI」）所顯示，該指數顯示在 2025 年幾乎每個月，調查之採購經理均報告活動減少，除了 1 月與 2 月，因指數低於成長門檻 50。2026 年 1 月則反轉此趨勢，指數高於成長門檻 52.6。另一方面，美國工業生產，報告年度工業部門營運產出，顯示 2025 年每個月均有成長，顯示雖然 PMI 建議 2025 年為廣泛收縮動能之年，但相較於前一年，整體產出仍具韌性。
根據金屬服務中心協會的資料，北美服務中心的業務量在2025年相比2024年下降了1.5%。同樣以北美為基準，Ryerson的業務量在相同期間下降了0.4%，表示本公司在該年度獲得了市場佔有率。從最終市場的業務量表現來看，Ryerson在商業運輸、氣候、重型機械與能源部門出現年增下降。這些下降部分被製造與焊接、機械工廠與機械與設備部門的需求成長所抵銷。

2026年2月13日（「閉市日」），本公司完成了根據2025年10月28日簽訂的合併協議（「合併協議」）所預期的交易，該協議由Ryerson Holding、Crimson MS Corp.（一家Ohio州公司，為Ryerson Holding的直接全資子公司（「合併子公司」））與Olympic Steel, Inc.（「Olympic Steel」）所簽訂。於閉市日，根據合併協議，合併子公司與Olympic Steel依照Ohio州法律合併。在Olympic Steel合併生效時，每張Olympic Steel普通股（每股無面額（「Olympic普通股」））（除外特定除外股份），轉換為取得1.7105張Ryerson Holding普通股，四捨五入至最近整數，以及現金抵換小數股。完成Olympic Steel合併後，Olympic Steel作為存續公司，成為Ryerson Holding的全資子公司。由於Olympic Steel合併，Ryerson Holding發行約19.5百萬張其普通股給Olympic普通股的原持有人。

Olympic Steel是一家專注於直接銷售與增值加工碳鋼與塗層鋼板、鋼片、鋼卷產品；不銹鋼鋼板、鋼片、鋼棒與鋼卷；鋁板、鋼片與鋼卷；管、管、棒、閥門與配件、錫板與金屬密集終端用途產品的金屬服務中心。兩家公司結合後，強化了Ryerson在北美第二大金屬服務中心的市場地位，將Olympic Steel的補充性據點、能力與產品組合納入Ryerson的智能互聯增值服務中心網路。合併後，作為Ryerson Holding Corporation運作，預計到2028年初將產生約120百萬美元的年度協同效益，透過採購規模、效率提升、商業增強與網路優化。請參閱第二部分，第8項「財務資料與補充資料」的附註19 — 「後續事件」，以取得更多關於Olympic Steel合併的資訊。
Ryerson的市場策略著重於以規模提供優質的客戶體驗。我們的文化基於我們的註冊商標口號「說是，然後解決」。我們致力於增加業務量，並透過增加製造業務、交易銷售與改善工具與分析的效率，來持續擴張邊際利益。Ryerson的財務策略包括專注於透過營運活動產生現金，並持續改善「週期性」營運模式，以維持強勁的資產負債表，重新投資業務成長，並為股東產生回報。

在2025年，繼歷史上高達三年的投資週期後，本公司專注於在Shelbyville, KY、Norcross, GA、Dallas, TX與Los Angeles, CA的服務中心進行主要資本投資專案的執行與優化。這些投資的主要目標是改善Ryerson的營運模式與客戶體驗。例如，Shelbyville服務中心的擴張是對明亮金屬平板加工能力的投資，以支持交易市場佔有率成長，同時以較低成本提供服務並提升服務水準。同樣地，Norcross、Dallas與Los Angeles的投資包括加工設備，我們預期這些設備將提高我們為客戶提供更高價值產品的能力，進而改善我們的毛利率。
2025年的需求情況持續低迷，同時價格波動，受關稅貿易政策影響。儘管如此，我們相信我們在服務能力與營運模式上的投資，將使我們能為客戶提供更好的體驗，進而為股東創造更大的價值。

headings: 總體經濟、市場趨勢及其他影響我們客戶獲利能力與財務穩定性的因素，已並可能繼續對我們的銷售成長與營運結果產生負面影響。
金屬服務業務競爭非常激烈，增加的競爭已並可能減少我們的營業收入與毛利率。
金屬價格的變動對我們的流動性、淨銷售額、毛利率、營運收入與淨收入有顯著影響。
未預期的產品短缺可能對客戶關係產生負面影響，進而對營運結果造成不利影響。
客戶或產品組成的變動可能導致我們的毛利率百分比下降。
如果北美製造業透過客戶產業中的併購或合併活動而衰退，我們可能無法維持或擴大客戶基礎。
全球金屬過度供給與金屬產品進口至美國，已並可能再次對美國金屬價格產生不利影響，這可能影響我們的銷售與營運結果。
如果我們失去其中一位主要供應商，我們的產品交貨時間與產品成本可能增加。
市場的波動可能導致 goodwill 產生重大減損。
通貨膨脹的變化已並可能繼續對財務表現產生不利影響。
我們可能無法成功整合本公司與 Olympic Steel 的業務，以實現 Olympic Steel 合併預期的效益，或在預期時間內完成此整合。
我們的部分營運位於美國境外，因此面臨與國際業務相關的風險。
我們可能因美國美元對加拿大幣、中國人民幣、香港幣及墨西哥比索的匯率波動而受到不利影響。
中國政府對我們必須如何進行業務活動有重大影響，特別是在我們設施所佔土地的使用方面。
資訊科技基礎建設的損壞可能對我們的業務造成損害。
我們面臨網路安全風險及其他可能因人工智慧的複雜性與使用率提高而產生的弱點，並可能因努力降低這些風險而產生增加的成本。
本公司或第三方使用或預期使用人工智慧技術，可能增加營運風險或產生新的或未預見的營運風險。
任何重大工廠停工都可能影響本公司業務。
某些員工退休福利計畫資金不足，這些福利的實際成本可能高於目前預估，這將需要本公司補足資金缺口。
任何持續的處理中心中斷都可能影響本公司業務。
若本公司無法留住、吸引並激勵管理階層及關鍵人員，可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司風險管理策略可能導致損失。
本公司可能因環境、健康及安全法規而產生重大成本。
環境、社會及治理議題，以及相關的報導義務，可能影響本公司業務。
稅制變更可能影響我們的稅務效益率、遞延稅資產價值以及未來獲利能力。
我們面臨訴訟風險，可能耗費我們的資源並分散管理階層的注意力。
我們可能面臨產品責任索償，這類索償可能成本高昂且造成不利的公眾聲譽。
我們的股票價格過去曾波動，近期表現波動，未來也可能波動，因此投資人持有我們普通股可能面臨重大損失。
我們在2025年每個季度都發放普通股現金股息，但未來是否發放股息則由我們董事會酌情決定。
我們的公司章程及特拉華州法律包含某些條款，可能阻礙、延宕或防止公司控制權的變更。
任何發行優先股的行為可能使其他公司難以取得我們，或可能以其他方式不利於我們普通股持有人，這可能壓低我們普通股的價格。
我們根據Ryerson信用融資安排負有債務，這可能不利於我們的財務狀況並使我們無法履行財務義務。
Ryerson Credit Facility 所包含的條件約束及未來我們所負擔債務之相關契約中所包含的條件約束，可能會施加限制，限制我們的營運與財務彈性。
我們可能無法產生足夠現金以償付所有債務。
由於我們所有債務之利率均會隨著某些現行短期利率的變動而浮動，因此我們會受到利率上升的影響。
我們信用評等及展望的變動可能會降低取得資金的管道，並提高借款成本。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨許多風險。您應仔細考量下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本報告中的其他資訊，包括合併財務報表與合併財務報表附註。本公司無法保證下列風險因素中所討論的任何事件不會發生。這些風險可能對本公司業務、營運成果、財務狀況與現金流產生重大且不利的影響。

經濟與產業趨勢會影響本公司業務環境。本公司服務多個金屬消費產業，這些產業對本公司產品與服務的需求，會受到客戶生產活動、資本支出與客戶產品與服務需求的影響。許多這些客戶營運的市場，會因季節性、市場不確定性、商品成本、匯率、外國競爭、生產外包、石油與天然氣價格、地緣政治發展以及許多其他我們無法控制的因素，而產生高度週期性波動。任何這些因素都已並可能導致客戶停工或關閉廠區、延後採購、降低生產量，或經驗到自身產品與服務需求的減少。
任何這些事件都可能影響客戶支付本公司應收款的能力，或降低客戶從本公司購買產品與服務的數量，並可能導致本公司銷售價格與銷售條件承受更大壓力。本公司不預期客戶羣體的週期性特質會改變，任何客戶產業的衰退都可能降低本公司收入與獲利，或美國、加拿大或其他主要經濟體，或任何這些經濟體的某個部門，出現顯著或持續的活動減緩，都可能對本公司銷售成長與營運成果產生負面影響。
我們在所服務的所有市場面臨競爭，從直接對特定客戶或市場區段銷售的金屬生產商，到其他金屬服務公司。金屬服務產業本身具有高度分散且競爭激烈的特性。雖然有少數大型競爭對手，但大多數市場由小型地方及區域性競爭對手服務。競爭主要基於價格、服務、品質、生產能力、存貨可得性及及時交貨。
我們正面臨來自線上企業的價格透明化競爭壓力。我們預期產業內的科技進步及電子商務解決方案的使用將持續以快速的步調發展。因此，我們要有效競爭的能力，需要我們回應並適應新的產業趨勢與發展，並實施新科技與創新，這可能會導致意外的成本，或耗時長於預期。
